title: How to check a firm or individual is authorised | FCA
text: Find out when you should use the Financial Services Register or FCA Firm Checker, what it means if you're using an appointed representative, and what to do if a firm is unauthorised. First published: 20/03/2023 Last updated: 03/09/2025 See all updates On this page How to check a firm or individual Using authorised firms What to do if a firm is unauthorised Products and services we do and don't regulate Firm information and contact details Appointed representatives In the UK, almost all firms that provide financial services must be authorised or registered by us. Being authorised means that firms must meet certain standards and have our permission to provide certain products and services. Being registered means that firms must meet certain requirements, but they don’t need to have our permission to provide products and services. Individuals who work at financial firms will sometimes need to be approved by us or certified at a firm to carry out financial activities as well. How to check a firm or individual There are different ways to check what firms and individuals can and can’t do. Not sure which service to use? Answer a few questions to find the information you need. Are you looking to check a firm or an individual? Back Firm > Individual > Use the Financial Services Register to: Find information on individuals working in financial services. Check the roles that individuals can perform now and have performed in the past. Find out where an individual previously worked. FCA employees are not listed on our FS Register (it's a record of the firms and individuals we authorise or register). Search the FS Register What do you want to check? Back I want to check a firm is genuine before I use them > If you’re looking to buy a financial product or service, you can use the Firm Checker to make sure the firm is authorised and has our permission to provide the services you’re looking for. Search the Firm Checker I want to check a firm I'm currently using > If you're looking to check if a firm was authorised when you first started dealing with them , use the FS Register . If you’re looking to buy a new financial product or service , use our Firm Checker to make sure the firm is authorised and has our permission to provide the services you’re looking for. I want to check a firm's full historical record > Use the Financial Services Register to find out whether a firm was previously authorised. Search the FS Register FCA Firm Checker Financial Service Register FCA Firm Checker You can use the Firm Checker before you buy a financial product or service, such as a mortgage, insurance or a funeral plan, for example. Checking a firm before you use them will help you avoid scams and will give you the best chance of protection if something goes wrong. Financial Service Register The FS Register is the official public record for all firms and individuals. It contains our full regulatory record for firms, individuals, and other bodies, with detailed information including: Historic fines. Firms' right to approve financial promotions. Firms' ability to handle client money. You should use the FS Register if you want to search for an individual or find out whether a firm was previously authorised. Using authorised firms Using an authorised firm, with the correct permissions, will greatly reduce the risk of harm. It won’t remove all risk. If you deal with a firm that isn't authorised or doesn't have permission for the activities you need, you won’t have access to the Financial Ombudsman Service if you want to complain. You also won’t be protected by the Financial Services Compensation Scheme (FSCS) if the firm goes out of business. This means it's unlikely you'd get your money back. What to do if a firm is unauthorised Some firms work without our authorisation. This is against the law. If we’ve published a warning about an unauthorised firm, this will appear on the FS Register and the Firm Checker when you search for the firm. Some unauthorised firms might be clone firms. A clone firm is a copy of a genuine, authorised firm. As part of a clone firm scam, fraudsters pretend to work for the authorised firm to con you. For a full list of the firms we’ve published warnings about, you can search our Warning List . Find out more about how to protect yourself from scams . No longer authorised or revoked firms On the FS Register, if you see a firm that's 'No longer authorised' or 'Revoked' it means the firm's authorisation has been cancelled and you should avoid dealing with it. These firms won’t appear on the Firm Checker unless they get authorised again. Show more + What it means if a firm is no longer authorised or revoked On the FS Register, when a firm shows as 'No longer authorised' or 'Revoked' it can no longer carry out any regulated financial activities. Firms can apply to voluntarily cancel their authorisation, for example, if they’re no longer carrying out any regulated activities. These firms appear on the FS register as ' No longer authorised '. However, some firms are cancelled following enforcement action. These firms appear on the FS Register as ' Revoked '. Some revoked firms may apply to have their authorisation reinstated (by applying for an annulment). But even if a firm does apply for an annulment, you should still avoid dealing with it unless its application is successful. Then its status on the FS Register and the Firm Checker will show as 'Authorised' again. You can check 'Disciplinary and regulatory action' on the firm’s FS Register page to find out why its authorisation was revoked. Show less - Products and services we do and don't regulate Financial firms offer a wide range of products and services, some of which we regulate, and some of which we don't. Firms we authorise can offer both regulated and unregulated products and services. But we have more limited powers over unregulated products and services. Below we've listed a few common types of financial products and services that we do and don't regulate. Learn more about financial services including mortgages, borrowing money, insurance and bank accounts by visiting MoneyHelper . Products and services we regulate Firms must be authorised by us to provide you with the following types of products and services. You should avoid using firms for the following services if they aren't authorised or don’t have the correct permissions: Bank accounts, for example, current and savings accounts. Lending money, including credit cards, hire, credit broking and debt advice. Debt-related services, including debt advice and debt collection. Crowdfunding platforms. Claims management services. Insurance (life insurance or general insurance, for example, for travel or your home). Funeral plans. Investments, for example, shares, funds and derivatives. Pensions, including workplace and personal pension plans. Home finance options, for example, residential mortgages, equity release or home purchase plans (including Sharia-compliant mortgages). Payments and e-money services, for example, online wallets and money transfers. For a full list of the activities we regulate, see the FCA Handbook . For more information on the types of activities that aren't in our current remit, see our perimeter report . Products and services we supervise Firms must be registered with us so we can supervise the following specific activities. You should avoid using firms for the following services if they aren't registered: Certain crypto activities, for example, crypto exchanges, crypto ATMs and custodian wallet providers (those crypto firms are registered with us for anti-money laundering purposes). Consumer buy-to-let mortgages (CBTL), for example, if you become an ‘accidental landlord’. Payments and e-money services provided by certain small firms. Products and services we don’t regulate or supervise There are other financial products and services that we don’t regulate or supervise shown below. Firms don't need to be authorised or registered to provide these: Unregulated Buy Now Pay Later (BNPL) . Advice on estate planning, wills and probate. Individual voluntary arrangements (IVAs) (an agreement between you and your lender to pay back your debts over a certain period). Debt collection of unpaid council tax, water, gas or electricity bills. Buy-to-let mortgages. Commercial mortgages and lending. Timeshares. Firm information and contact details On the FS Register and Firm Checker, we show whether firms are authorised or registered, and what products and services they're allowed to offer. But the firm's contact details are provided and confirmed by the firm. This includes the firm's: Registered name and other trading names. Main place of business. Complaint contact details. Appointed representatives (if applicable). Most firms we authorise must update or confirm their contact information, at least once a year . You'll be able to see if a firm has confirmed its contact details on the FS Register and Firm Checker. Principal firms will do this on behalf of their appointed representatives. Appointed representatives You may notice that some firms on the FS Register and the Firm Checker are listed as appointed representatives (ARs) . This means they’re carrying out activities on behalf of another firm, known as their principal . ARs can have more than one principal. The principal agrees what activities the AR can do and is responsible for that business. It’s important you check with the principal if you have concerns about an AR or the products and services it can offer. If an AR has gone beyond the activities the principal has allowed, you may not be protected by the Financial Ombudsman or the FSCS if something goes wrong. You can find contact details for ARs and principals on the FS Register and the Firm Checker. You can ask the principal to confirm what activities the AR has permission for and how you'd be protected if something went wrong.
